title: Ephesus: Paul, Artemis & Roman Asia
subtitle: Urban archaeology and ministry geography without invented addresses
summary: Explore established Ephesus, its Great Theater and Artemision, Paul’s city-level ministry setting, and Revelation’s Ephesian context while keeping the Hall of Tyrannus and individual meeting houses unlocated.
disclaimer: Ephesus, the Great Theater, and Artemision are securely located. The Hall of Tyrannus remains unpinned. This prototype uses the modern map/coastline as reference and does not draw an unverified first-century harbor shoreline or reconstruct individual buildings beyond established archaeological locations.

evidenceLegend.label: Physical terrain
evidenceLegend.description: Measured terrain only when a verified DEM is configured; otherwise the map remains a geographic reference surface.

evidenceLegend.label: Known archaeology
evidenceLegend.description: Excavated or independently established places/features represented only at the precision supported by existing atlas records.

evidenceLegend.label: Historical interpretation
evidenceLegend.description: Textual or scholarly historical context that does not by itself identify a specific excavated structure or event point.

evidenceLegend.label: Later tradition
evidenceLegend.description: A later commemorative or reception-history identification kept distinct from first-century or ancient evidence.

evidenceLegend.label: Unknown / disputed
evidenceLegend.description: A building, route, event point, or interpretive identification that cannot responsibly be fixed to an exact coordinate.

periods.label: Roman city
periods.note: Orients the established city, theater, and Artemision in the Roman-period landscape without a full architectural reconstruction.

camera.note: City-scale view anchored on established Ephesus archaeology; not a first-century eye-level viewpoint.

periods.label: Pauline ministry
periods.note: Frames Acts 18–20 at city level; Paul’s lecture hall, residence, and exact movement through streets remain unknown.

camera.note: Centers Ephesus as the secure ministry setting, not the Hall of Tyrannus.

periods.label: Revelation context
periods.note: Shows Ephesus as one of the historical Seven Churches while leaving Revelation’s visionary entities in the separate visionary system.

camera.note: Historical city context only; no visionary geography is projected onto the city.

entryCamera.note: Centers the established archaeological city and its nearby major sanctuary landscape.

comparison.label: Ephesus lens
comparison.intro: The city is secure; individual ministry addresses are not. Use these lenses to separate archaeological anchors from textual urban activity.

options.label: Urban archaeology
options.summary: Ephesus, the theater, and Artemision are established archaeological anchors.
options.rationale: These places can be mapped at site level without reconstructing every first-century street or building.
options.objections: A verified period coastline/harbor reconstruction is still pending.

options.label: Paul’s ministry
options.summary: Acts securely names Ephesus as Paul’s extended ministry setting; the Hall of Tyrannus is not archaeologically located.
options.rationale: City-level geography can be shown without inventing the lecture hall or house-church addresses.
options.objections: No current excavated building is promoted here as the Hall of Tyrannus.

camera.note: Centers Ephesus as the secure city setting; it does not locate the Hall of Tyrannus.

options.label: Artemis + theater
options.summary: The Artemision and Great Theater provide independently known civic/religious context for Acts 19.
options.rationale: Acts names the theater assembly and Artemis cult context, both of which can be connected to securely identified sites.
options.objections: Acts does not say Paul entered the Artemision or identify his position inside the theater.

camera.note: Frames both established sites together; no route between them is asserted.

hotspots.label: Ephesus
hotspots.summary: Securely identified Roman Asian city central to Acts 18–20 and one of Revelation’s Seven Churches.

whyShown.evidence: Ancient Ephesus is securely identified and extensively excavated.
whyShown.inference: The city-level setting can anchor Acts and Revelation without assigning every narrative moment to a building.
whyShown.alternatives: Ancient shoreline and harbor configuration require verified geomorphological/archaeological data before being drawn.

hotspots.label: Great Theater of Ephesus
hotspots.summary: Established theater associated with the civic assembly in Acts 19.

whyShown.evidence: The Great Theater is securely located and fits the civic venue named in Acts 19.
whyShown.inference: The connection is at venue level, not seat or participant position.
whyShown.alternatives: No seat-by-seat reconstruction of the disturbance is claimed.

hotspots.label: Temple of Artemis / Artemision
hotspots.summary: Established major sanctuary central to Ephesian identity and Acts 19’s religious/economic context.

whyShown.evidence: The Artemision site is securely identified archaeologically.
whyShown.inference: Its presence explains the wider civic/religious setting of Acts 19.
whyShown.alternatives: Acts does not place Paul inside the sanctuary.
